subject.title: UI/TUI: session-recap block leaks into visible user message rendering

question: Should maintainers wait for the conflicting, non-maintainer-modifiable fork PR at https://github.com/BingqingLyu/openclaw/pull/252, or replace it with a maintainer-owned narrow fix for this still-source-reproducible bug?
rationale: The bug and fix boundary are clear, but the only open implementation candidate is outside the target repository's normal maintainer-edit path and cannot currently merge cleanly.

options.title: Replace the fork PR
options.body: Open or adopt a narrow maintainer-editable PR in the target repository, credit the existing fork work, and close or supersede the fork PR after the replacement exists.

options.title: Ask for a rebase
options.body: Keep the issue paired with the fork PR and ask the contributor to rebase it onto current main with maintainer-editable settings if possible.

options.title: Wait without action
options.body: Leave both items open until the contributor updates the fork PR, accepting that the known source-reproducible bug remains unresolved meanwhile.

recommendation.title: Replace the fork PR
recommendation.body: Open or adopt a narrow maintainer-editable PR in the target repository, credit the existing fork work, and close or supersede the fork PR after the replacement exists.

likelyOwner.reason: They merged the original shared sanitizer path and authored the TUI leading-stripper follow-up, so they are the strongest routing candidate for choosing adoption versus replacement.
